newsitem.title: FRANCE: France may sell Air France, C.Lyonnais this year.
newsitem.headline: France may sell Air France, C.Lyonnais this year.

text.p: France may privatise Air France and possibly state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais this year, French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said in an interview with business daily Les Echos.
In the interview, to be published on Thursday, he noted that the sales of defence electronics company Thomson-CSF and France Telecom were already under way.
These would be followed by insurer GAN and its banking arm CIC. "CIC and GAN will follow," he said .
"In the course of the year we should continue that of Aerospatiale-Dassault, and undertake, if possible, that of Air France and maybe that of Credit Lyonnais," he said.
The government had previously said it did not plan to sell Credit Lyonnais until late 1998 or early 1999.
The bank has staged a strong recovery after suffering heavy losses between 1992 and 1994.
Air France chairman Christian Blanc had previously said he would like the airline to be privatised by the end of the year.
Opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin accused Juppe's government of using state sell-offs simply to plug the public finances and urged better balance between markets and the state.
"They need to privatise companies only to balance their budget. It's an admission of failure," he said in an interview on TF1 television.

The Socialist party, campaigning ahead of a two-round parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1, has vowed to halt privatisations including the partial sale of France Telecom, in which the government plans to sell a 30-35 percent stake.
Jospin however appeared to soften his stance on this sale earlier this week by telling a newspaper he would consult the staff on reports that some of them favour partial privatisation.
